title: ModelConfig
description: One entry in the model registry: what to load, how to feed it, and how to read what comes out.
$comment:
OWNERSHIP: Claude owns registry contents (these files), Codex owns the loader in workers/ml-runtime. The format is therefore a cross-boundary interface and is validated in CI on both sides.

 WHY PRE/POST-PROCESSING IS PART OF THE REGISTRY AND NOT THE RUNTIME CODE:
 a model swap that silently changes normalisation changes every score in the library, and nothing about it looks like a bug. It looks like the taste model drifting. Pinning the exact input size, colour order, mean/std and output layout next to the weights hash means a swap is a diff, and a wrong swap fails a golden test rather than quietly degrading a year of rankings.

 LICENCE STATUS IS REQUIRED ON EVERY ENTRY. A model may be loaded for development while its licence is unresolved -- that is a legitimate stage -- but the registry has to say so, so that 'we will deal with licensing later' stays a decision someone can act on rather than something that ships by forgetting.

model_id.description: Stable slug. Matches ModelRef.model_id in the contract, so a score can be traced to the exact registry entry that produced it.

runtime_targets.description: Execution providers this entry is known to work on, best first. The loader picks the first available. Listing a target is a claim that it has been run, not that it ought to work.

outputs.description: Every output tensor, named and shaped. The loader binds by name; a model whose output names change is a different entry, not the same one upgraded.

allOf.$comment:
SAFETY CLASSIFIER: THE CLASS AXIS IS PINNED, NOT DESCRIBED.

Issue #21, and the defect docs/safety-classifier-decision.md §6.6 raised: the placeholder declared `sensitive_logits` with shape [-1, 3] and nothing anywhere said which index was which class. Transpose two columns and every breastfeeding photograph classifies as explicit, with no test failing anywhere in the stack -- the scores stay in [0,1], the threshold still fires, the manifest still validates, and the only signal is a family's photograph quietly missing from their album.

So for a `safety_classifier` entry every logits/scores output must carry EXACTLY the contract's three classes in the contract's order. `contracts/schemas/safety-clearance.schema.json` pins the same three strings as a const on `ClassifierPin.class_order`, so a config edited here can no longer produce a manifest that validates there. Not a convention, not a comment: two schemas that have to agree.

What this cannot express is `len(class_order) == shape[-1]` -- JSON Schema cannot compare an array's length to an element of a sibling array. That equality is checked in models/tests/test_model_registry.py and again at load time in packages/safety-gate/memory_engine_safety/head.py.

source_url.description: Where the weights come from. Null ONLY for rollout.state 'placeholder' -- a slot the product needs where no checkpoint has been chosen. Enforced: a null source_url with any other rollout state is invalid, so an entry cannot be promoted with no checkpoint provenance. A URL whose last path segment is a file name (or a Hugging Face /resolve/ URL) is a fetchable ARTIFACT and scripts/models/fetch_weights.py downloads it; anything else is a provenance page only, and the fetcher reports the entry unavailable rather than saving a web page as a model.

archive_member.description: Path inside the archive at source_url that holds these weights, when the publisher ships a bundle rather than a bare file. Null when source_url is the artifact itself. `filename` stays the name the file is installed and loaded under, so a bundle member may be renamed on install -- det_10g.onnx becomes scrfd_10g_bnkps.onnx. This exists because the member used to be written into source_url as a parenthetical, which no fetcher could act on.

blake3.description: Hash of the exact bytes. Null means UNPINNED: the file has not been downloaded and hashed yet, so this entry is not reproducible and must not be promoted past `candidate`. 'The same version' of a HuggingFace repo has had its weights changed underneath people before.

conversion.description: Present when NO PUBLISHER SHIPS THIS ARTIFACT and we produce it ourselves. Issue #79: google/siglip2-so400m-patch14-384 publishes safetensors only, so `filename` names a file that exists on no server and the fetcher would have gone on reporting the entry unavailable forever. A conversion nobody else can reproduce is worse than none, so this block names the exact input (an immutable URL plus its SHA-256) and the script in this repository that turns it into the artifact. `scripts/models/fetch_weights.py` reads this and reports the entry CONVERTIBLE with the command to run, instead of downloading `input_url` and installing the conversion INPUT under the artifact's name. It is not a substitute for `blake3`: the input is pinned here, the output is pinned there, and only a human writes the latter.

script.description: Repository-relative path of the script that produces the artifact. Must exist; a conversion whose script was deleted is a claim of reproducibility that is no longer true.

input_url.description: The exact file converted, at an immutable revision. A branch name would let the input change under the digest that describes the output.

input_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the bytes at `input_url`, checked by the conversion script before it builds anything. SHA-256 rather than BLAKE3 because publishers state SHA-256 -- Hugging Face's LFS oid is one -- so this digest can be compared against the source's own record instead of only against ourselves.

toolchain.description: What produced the artifact, in enough detail to explain why a re-run's bytes differ. Byte-identical re-export is not claimed: the graph is emitted by whatever PyTorch is installed. What is reproducible is the input and the procedure.

then.$comment: No source means no artifact, so a hash, byte size, archive member or conversion recipe alongside a null source_url is describing a file that does not exist.
A converted artifact is built, not extracted. An archive member alongside a conversion recipe describes two different ways of obtaining the same file, and the fetcher would have to pick one.

Preprocessing.title: Preprocessing
Preprocessing.description: Exactly how a proxy becomes a tensor. Every field here changes model output, and a mismatch is silent -- the model still returns plausible numbers.

resize.description: How the source is fitted to the model input. `longest_side` limits the LONGER dimension to `resize_limit` and preserves aspect, which is what detectors with dynamic input shapes do; it is not letterbox, because there is no padding and therefore no padded region to dilute a coverage measure.

color_order.description: RGB vs BGR is the single most common silent preprocessing bug. InsightFace models want BGR; almost everything else wants RGB.

scale.description: Multiplier applied before mean subtraction, e.g. 1/255 for models expecting [0,1].

face_alignment.description: For face_crop inputs: the canonical landmark template the crop is warped onto. Alignment is not optional for recognition -- an unaligned crop produces an embedding that is confidently wrong.

sequence_length.description: For image_sequence models such as shot detection.

resize_limit.description: Pixel limit for the resize mode that needs one (`longest_side`, `shortest_side`). PP-OCRv4 detection uses 960.

size_multiple.description: Round both dimensions to a multiple of this after resizing. Fully convolutional detectors require it (PP-OCRv4 uses 32) because the feature-map strides do not divide arbitrary sizes -- getting it wrong changes the output grid rather than raising.

pad_value.description: What the padded band CONTAINS, for any resize mode that pads. Issue #33. The geometry was pinned and the contents were not: a 16:9 image letterboxed into 640x640 has 280 padded rows, and 0 vs 127.5 vs the dataset mean send materially different tensors through the network -- for YuNet, whose scale is 1 with no mean or std, the difference between a band of 0.0 and a band of 127.5 in the tensor itself. Detections near the image edge change and nothing raises. Null means UNRESOLVED, not zero: an entry whose upstream sources disagree about the value must say so and be refused by the load gate, because a wrongly pinned value is worse than an absent one. Required whenever `resize` is `letterbox`, so it cannot be defaulted by omission.

allOf.$comment: MISSING must fail validation; only an explicit null may say 'unresolved'. An absent field would be indistinguishable from a decision nobody made, which is how the runtime came to invent black padding in the first place.

PadValue.title: PadValue
PadValue.description: The pixel value written into the padded band, and where it came from.

space.description: WHERE IN THE PIPELINE THE VALUE IS APPLIED, which is not cosmetic. `pixel` means the band is filled before normalisation and then normalised with everything else, so it lands at (value * scale - mean) / std. `normalized` means the band is written directly into the finished tensor. mmdetection's test pipelines normalise and THEN pad with 0, which is a band of 0.0 in tensor units -- equivalent to a pixel value of the mean, not of black. Recording only the number would collapse those two into one and pick the wrong one half the time.

values.description: One value applied to every channel, or one per channel in the order the tensor stores them (i.e. after any RGB/BGR swap).

source.description: The upstream artifact this was read out of -- file and symbol, not 'the docs'. A citation nobody can follow is indistinguishable from a guess, and this field exists because the previous guess looked exactly like a decision.

template.description: Destination landmark coordinates in the aligned crop, in pixels. A similarity transform maps the detected landmarks onto these.

steps.description: Ordered. `l2_normalize` on an embedding is required, not cosmetic: every VectorSpace in the contract stores normalised vectors and cosine distance assumes it.

normalisation.description: How a raw model score becomes the [0,1] Unit the contract stores. Required wherever a Score is written, because fusion must never need to know a model's native range.

landmark_scheme.description: Which LandmarkScheme this detector emits, matching the proto enum and FaceRecord.Landmarks.scheme. Required for any detector producing landmarks: five points in ArcFace order and five points in YuNet order produce a plausible warp and a wrong embedding, and without this the host would need a per-model-id hardcode -- defeating a registry-driven loader.

max_detections.description: Cap on emitted detections, post-NMS. Backs DetectionSet.truncated: without a configured cap the host has nothing to report truncation against, and silently returning the top N reads downstream as 'there were exactly N faces'.

top_k.description: PRE-NMS candidate cap. YuNet applies one and it changes the output, so leaving it unpinned means two hosts can legitimately disagree while both matching the config.

shape.description: Dimensions, with -1 for dynamic. Documented so a shape change is caught at load rather than producing garbage downstream.

dimensions.description: For embeddings: the vector width. Must match the VectorSpace it is written into.

vector_space.description: Which contract VectorSpace this embedding belongs to. Two vectors are only comparable when this matches exactly, including the model version.

stride.description: Feature-map stride this output belongs to, for multi-level detectors. Required to interpret an export whose tensor names carry no meaning: SCRFD's published graph names its outputs 448/451/454..., and without the stride the host cannot tell which anchor grid a row indexes. The row count must equal (input/stride)^2 * anchors, which is what makes the declaration checkable rather than asserted.

class_order.description:
The class each column of the LAST axis means, in order. Null for any output whose last axis is not a class axis.

Same defect as `stride` and `landmark_scheme`, in the place where it costs the most. A tensor of shape [-1, 3] carries no labels; whoever writes the host decides what column 0 means, and if they decide wrongly nothing raises -- the numbers stay in range, the thresholds still fire, and the wrong photographs get blocked or cleared. `stride` exists because SCRFD's outputs are named 448/451/454; this exists because a safety head's are named nothing at all.

Must have exactly one entry per column: `len(class_order) == shape[-1]`. JSON Schema cannot compare an array's length to a number inside a sibling array, so that equality is enforced in code -- models/tests/test_model_registry.py, and again at load in packages/safety-gate. The conditional at the root of this schema pins the strings and their order for `safety_classifier` entries, where a transposition is a user-visible harm rather than a quality regression.

Batching.title: Batching
Batching.description: What the CHECKPOINT can do, not what the product would like. Issue #31: YuNet declared supported/max_batch 8/dynamic_axes true against a graph whose input is fixed at [1,3,640,640]; a batch of 2 fails ONNX Runtime dimension validation. Five of nine configs carried a dynamic-batching claim and not one of them said where the claim came from, so an assumption and a measurement were indistinguishable in a diff. `verified_against` is the fix: a capability claim beyond one-at-a-time must cite what established it.

dynamic_axes.description: Whether the BATCH axis is dynamic. Not spatial dynamism: a model can take any height and width while its batch dimension is fixed at 1, which is true of both MUSIQ and PP-OCRv4. Variable input SIZE is expressed by `preprocessing.input_size: null` with `resize_limit` and `size_multiple`. Conflating the two makes a host either batch a model that cannot be batched, or refuse to resize one that must be.

verified_against.description: How the claim above was established -- the checkpoint inspected and the tool that reported its input shape. Null is the honest state for an unverified entry, and null forces `supported: false`, `max_batch: 1`, `dynamic_axes: false`, because an unverified capability claim is exactly the defect. Getting this wrong is not silent at inference -- ONNX Runtime raises on a bad leading dimension -- but the CONFIG is silent, and the host clamping to the real graph is what let a wrong config survive review.

allOf.$comment: Any claim beyond 'one at a time' needs a citation. Declining to batch costs throughput; claiming a batch axis that is not there costs a whole inference pass with an error nobody expected in a background worker.

LicenseStatus.title: LicenseStatus
LicenseStatus.description: Required on every entry. A model may be used in development with an unresolved licence -- that is a real stage of a real project -- but the registry must say so out loud, so deferring the decision stays a decision rather than an omission.

weights_license.description: Separate from the code licence on purpose. This is the field that catches InsightFace: MIT code, non-commercial weights.

verified.description: True only when a human read the current licence at the source and recorded the date. Never set by inference.

training_data.description: Dataset provenance. A permissively-licensed model can still be trained on a retracted dataset (MS-Celeb-1M, VGGFace2), which is a separate exposure from the model licence and is invisible unless recorded here.

blocks_commercial_release.description: True when shipping commercially with this entry would be a licence violation. The build can use it; a commercial release must not. Checked in tests.

state.description: `placeholder` means the config records a SHAPE, not a runnable model: the checkpoint is unselected or its export is unverified. It is a load-gate input, not documentation -- the gate refuses it in every mode, because a placeholder whose weights file happens to exist would otherwise load and return plausible numbers from constants nobody checked.
